nodes.name: Co-precipitation of SCOH
nodes.procedure: 2 mmol CoCl2·6H2O were dissolved in 0.3 M sodium citrate aqueous solution and stirred for 30 min. The solution was cooled down below 273 K before subsequent operation. Then, 10 mL of 0.2 M SnCl4 aqueous solution was dropped in the cooled solution and stirred for another 30 min. After that, 2 M NaOH solution was added to the above solution drop by drop until the pH value was tuned to 10, and more 30 min stirring was maintained to obtain pink-colored precipitates. The pink-colored precipitates were washed with water and ethanol several times and dried in a vacuum oven at 333 K for 24 hours.

nodes.name: Pyrolysis to A-SCOH
nodes.procedure: The prepared SnCo(OH)6 was further annealed at 573 K in H2/Ar (5%/95%) atmosphere for 30 min to obtain amorphous-SnCo(OH)6 (labeled as A-SCOH).

nodes.name: Ion exchange and pyrolysis to A-RSCOH
nodes.procedure: 25 mg A-SCOH was dispersed in deionized (DI) water. Moderate RuCl3·xH2O (0.02, 0.03, 0.04, 0.05 mmol) was added to 10 ml DI water to obtain a homogeneous solution and then dropped into the above suspension under stirring conditions. The ion exchange-pyrolysis sustained for a while (2 ~ 8 h) at room temperature, the product was collected after washing by DI water and ethanol and dried at 333 K overnight (generated sample is labeled as H-RSCOH). Finally, the dried precipitate was pyrolyzed at 573 K for 4 h (generated sample labeled as A-RSCOH).

nodes.characterization_summary: SCOH shows characteristic peaks of perovskite-type cobalt-tin hydroxide (JCPDS: 13-0356). A-SCOH and A-RSCOH show no XRD peaks, confirming amorphous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern is shown in Supplementary Fig. 1, and the representative peaks of SCOH are attributed to the perovskite-type cobalt-tin hydroxide (JCPDS: 13-0356). After calcining under a reducing atmosphere, the characteristic peaks of SnCo(OH)₆ disappear, indicating the amorphous structure of A-SCOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: SCOH, A-SCOH, and A-RSCOH show numerous accumulations of nanocubes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Numerous accumulations of SCOH nanocubes are observed in the SEM images, and this is maintained for A-SCOH and A-RSCOH (Supplementary Figs. 2–7 and Fig. 1a).

nodes.characterization_summary: SCOH shows nanocube morphology. A-SCOH shows softened nanocube morphology compared to SCOH. No obvious difference between A-SCOH and A-RSCOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the TEM images in Supplementary Figs. 8–12, the shape of the nanocube morphology for A-SCOH becomes softened compared with the pristine SCOH, while no obvious difference between A-SCOH and A-RSCOH is discovered (Fig. 1bc).

nodes.characterization_summary: A-SCOH and A-RSCOH confirmed amorphous structure. SCOH shows lattice distance of 0.234 nm for (311) facet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) images confirmed the amorphous structure of A-SCOH and A-RSCOH (Fig. 1d and Supplementary Figs. 10, 12). For the distinct lattice fringe in Supplementary Fig. 8, the lattice distance of 0.234 nm for SCOH can be indexed to the (311) facet.

nodes.characterization_summary: Homogeneous elemental distribution of each element in nanocubes of SCOH, A-SCOH, and A-RSCOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping of SCOH, A-SCOH, and A-RSCOH are shown in Supplementary Figs. 1–11 and Fig. 1e, revealing that each element is distributed homogeneously in the nanocubes.

nodes.characterization_summary: A-RSCOH Co 2p3/2 at 781.3 eV and 2p1/2 at 796.8 eV (Co²⁺), additional peaks at 780.1/795.9 eV (Co³⁺); Sn 3d5/2 at 486.6 eV (Sn⁴⁺); O 1s at 529.8 eV (M-O), 531.1 eV (M-OH), 532.5 eV (adsorbed H₂O); Ru 3p3/2 at 463.7/466.4 eV (Ru³⁺/⁴⁺ mix). Co 2p shifts positively vs A-SCOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS peaks at 781.3 (2p3/2) and 796.8 eV (2p1/2) with satellite peaks of A-RSCOH are shown in Supplementary Fig. 14a, corresponding to the Co²⁺. In addition, two XPS peaks at 780.1 and 795.9 eV emerged, which are ascribed to Co³⁺. According to the highresolution XPS spectrum of Sn3d, the peak for Sn 3d5/2 (486.6 eV) of A-RSCOH is attributed to the Sn⁴⁺.

nodes.characterization_summary: A-RSCOH Ru K-edge XANES similar to RuO₂ (Ru⁴⁺), EXAFS Ru-O at 1.52 Å (no Ru-Ru); Co K-edge XANES ~Co(OH)₂ (Co²⁺), EXAFS Co-O at 1.46 Å; coordination numbers Co-O and Ru-O ~5.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra of the Ru K-edge are shown in Supplementary Fig. 15a... similar to RuO₂, demonstrating the valence state of Ru in A-RSCOH is approximately +4. From the analysis of the Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectroscopy of A-RSCOH... a first shell at 1.52 Å of Ru-O is discovered.

nodes.characterization_summary: A-RSCOH shows increased effective magnetic moment μ_eff compared to SCOH and A-SCOH, reflecting quantum spin interaction of Ru and Co.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The effective magnetic moment (μ_eff) of electrocatalysts... Compared with SCOH and A-SCOH, the obvious increase in μ_eff for A-RSCOH reflects an increase in the number of unpaired d electrons, demonstrating the quantum spin interaction of Ru and Co.

nodes.characterization_summary: A-RSCOH shows Co²⁺→Co³⁺ at 0.9 V (420 nm), Co³⁺→Co⁴⁺ at 1.20 V (580 nm), high-valent Co at 1.3 V (525 nm), occurring at lower potentials than SCOH and A-SCOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A broad peak centered at approximately 420 nm emerges for A-RSCOH at 0.9 V, which is attributed to the oxidation of Co²⁺ to Co³⁺... For A-RSCOH, another increase in absorbance at approximately 580 nm is observed at 1.20 V and above.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine A-RSCOH/A-SCOH show Co-O at 510 cm⁻¹, Co-OH at 623 cm⁻¹. After solvation, peaks at 508, 602, 674 cm⁻¹ for amorphous CoOOH. At 1.2 V and above, peaks shift to 487, 572, 680 cm⁻¹ for disordered CoO₂ phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra of pristine A-SCOH and A-RSCOH have two Raman peaks at 510 and 623 cm⁻¹, which are the characteristic peaks of Co-O and Co-OH bonds... The final peaks are ascribed to the vibrational modes of disordered the CoO₂ phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance C_dl of A-RSCOH is 0.01 mF cm⁻², larger than SCOH (0.002 mF cm⁻²) and A-SCOH (0.008 mF cm⁻²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: A-RSCOH has a C_dl of 0.01 mF cm⁻², which is larger than that of SCOH (0.002 mF cm⁻²) and A-SCOH (0.008 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: A-RSCOH shows smallest charge transfer resistance among catalysts from Nyquist plots.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3e, the smallest charge transfer resistance of A-RSCOH is obtained from the Nyquist plots, indicating the notable electroconductibility and charge transfer kinetics of A-RSCOH.
